statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-4224: when an Expat parser with a registered ElementDeclHandler parses an inline document type definition with a deeply nested content model, conv_content_model() in the pyexpat module recursed without bound and could overflow the C stack. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/145986 (3.10 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/af856a7177326ac25d9f66cc6dd28b554d914fee), first released in CPython 3.10.21; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/5M7CGUW3XBRY7II4DK43KF7NQQ3TPZ6R/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-4224, which lists every 3.10 release before 3.10.21 as affected. The fix wraps conv_content_model() in a recursion guard whose message, ' in conv_content_model', appears in Modules/pyexpat.c of CPython 3.10.21 and 3.10.22 and not in 3.10.19 or 3.10.20. Searched the pyexpat extension module in the python-3.10 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-28, 3.10.19-r0 to 3.10.22-r8, on x86_64 and aarch64 (package sizes checked against the repository index) for that message, with the module's ElementDeclHandler string as the positive control, which every module contains: the modules in 3.10.19-r0, 3.10.20-r0 and 3.10.20-r1 do not contain it, and every module from 3.10.20-r2 to 3.10.22-r8 does, on both architectures. The range ends at 3.10.20-r2.

CVE-2026-4224: when an Expat parser with a registered ElementDeclHandler parses an inline document type definition with a deeply nested content model, conv_content_model in the pyexpat module recursed without bound and could overflow the C stack. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/145986; the 3.12 branch fix is https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/24ce88b285f56ee11626cf5e472af3cd8cc7c621, first released in CPython 3.12.14 (https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31214/); see also https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/5M7CGUW3XBRY7II4DK43KF7NQQ3TPZ6R/. Checked the pyexpat extension module shipped in the python-3.12 package of all 24 published builds in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, on x86_64 and aarch64, for the recursion guard the fix adds to conv_content_model (its ' in conv_content_model' recursion message), with the module's ElementDeclHandler string as the positive control, which every module contains. The 3.12.12-r0, 3.12.13-r0 and 3.12.13-r1 modules lack it and contain no conv_content_model string at all. 3.12.13-r2 is the first published build that has it, as a backport onto CPython 3.12.13, and every later build carries it, including the builds of the upstream 3.12.14, 3.12.15 and 3.12.16 releases.

CVE-2026-4224: An Expat parser with a registered ElementDeclHandler recursed without bound in pyexpat when converting a deeply nested content model in an inline document type definition, so a crafted document could overflow the C stack. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/145986 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e0a8a6da90597a924b300debe045cdb4628ee1f3), first released in CPython 3.14.4; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/5M7CGUW3XBRY7II4DK43KF7NQQ3TPZ6R/; https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-4224. Checked the pyexpat extension module in every published build, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package on x86_64 and aarch64 for the recursion guard the fix adds to conv_content_model (its ' in conv_content_model' recursion message). 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.3-r1 lack the fix; 3.14.4-r1 is the first published build that has it and is built from the upstream 3.14.4 release, and every later build carries it.
